messages.subject: ddply with empty data frame and .drop=FALSE causes unexpected results (?)
messages.subject_clean: ddply with empty data frame and .drop=FALSE causes unexpected results (?)
messages.body_plain:
Hi all, I'm fairly new to both R and plyr, and have been using subset and ddply in a variety of contexts (usually embedded within functions with a variety of arguments). What I have found is that when I use subset and get to an empty data frame, and pass that through to data frame, I get a result that seems to be inconsistent with the rest of ddply's returns.

To demonstrate [1]:
> > data(ToothGrowth)
> > (x <- subset(ToothGrowth, subset=(len==4.2 & supp=="VC")))
>   len supp dose
> 1 4.2   VC  0.5
> > (y <- subset(ToothGrowth, subset=(len==4.2 & supp=="OJ")))
> [1] len  supp dose
> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
> > ddply(x, .(supp), nrow, .drop=FALSE)
>   supp V1
> 1   OJ  0
> 2   VC  1
> > ddply(y, .(supp), nrow, .drop=FALSE)
> [1] len  supp dose
> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

(1) I would expect ddply(y, .(supp), nrow, .drop=FALSE) to actually return
  supp V1
1   OJ  0
2   VC  0

(2) and even expect ddply(y, .(supp), nrow, .drop=TRUE) to return
> [1] supp V1
> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
rather than
> [1] len  supp dose
> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

I'm switching to using the table function for this simple case, but I just wanted to point this out here as what seems to be behavior that doesn't live up to the consistency of rest of plyr.

No - you need to use ddply from the plyr package instead:

> ap2 <- dcast(ap1, subject + Group ~ Length + Complexity + variable,
> fun.aggregate = mean)

ddply(ap1, c("subject", "Group", "Length", "Complexity"), summarise,
  mean = mean(variable),
  median = median(variable)

It's possible this might be easier to do in the tables package
(http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/tables/index.html), since it
looks like you're interested in creating a table for display, rather
than a dataset for further analysis.

messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I have what seems like a super simple problem but I can't seem to
figure out the right search terms. I need to summarize some data but I
would like to keep the variables that I am not using to as groups in
the resulting data frames. For example say I have the following
dataframe:

dat1 <- data.frame(x = runif(2190, 0, 125), year=rep(1995:2000,
each=365), jday=1:365, site="here")
dat2 <- data.frame(x = runif(2190, 0, 200), year=rep(1995:2000,
each=365), jday=1:365, site="there")
dat <- rbind(dat1,dat2)
str(dat)

## I want the max value of x for each group ("site") for all year
## No problem, I can do this using ddply like so

library(plyr)
ddply(dat, c("site"), function(df) return(c(max=max(df$x))))

## Now problem is that I also want to know what year and what jday
corresponds to this max value.
## So my question is: How do I keep these variables in my resulting dataframe?

Thanks so much in advance!

Sam

Hi:

One problem with your function is that it doesn't return anything,
which is why you got the unexpected result. Here's an alternative
approach that's a little shorter:

offrank <- function(d) {
    # make a table of party membership, coerce it to a numeric vector
    v <- as.vector(table(d$party))
    # orders by ascending g if v[1] >= v[2] (more d's) and descending o/w
    u <- if(v[1] >= v[2]) d[order(d$g), ] else d[order(-d$g), ]
    # grab the 12th row and return
    tail(head(u, 12), 1)
   }

> with(foo, table(comm, party))
    party
comm  d  r
   1 11  9
   2 12  8
   3 11  9

highest ranking r
> ddply(foo, .(comm), offrank)
  comm official party          g
1    1       17     r  0.3068895
2    2        2     d  0.1550925
3    3        5     r -0.1013725

I'd recommend doing this in two steps.  First compute the rank
variable and the subset based on that - that will make it much easier
to check your logic:

foo <- ddply(foo, "comm", mutate,
  adjust = ifelse(mean(party == "d") > 0.5, 1, -1),
  rank = rank(adjust * g)
)
subset(foo, rank == 12)

messages.body_plain:
I am dissatisfied with the current summary statistics for a data.frame.  I want to be able to specify the summary statistics for the table that I want computed not just the defaults for the class.  I came across this problem recently with creating a demographics table.  So I fixed it.

 I created a function that can be passes to ldply and have functions specified as the extra arguments and produce a data frame with the summary statistics.  Functions must take a vector and return a vector.  Names can be optionally specified.  You can see it at  https://gist.github.com/1711802.

I can't help but think this sort of thing probably already exists, but I could not find it, and it was just a few minutes to write up.  Aggregate gets close but not quite.  Either way it is a useful function for plyr.

Thanks,
Andrew
